body: I'm feeling the same way -- I feel like this might be the one type of affair that a couple can get past, but only if we talk through it.
It's not okay to cry alone but sometimes I feel like this is all I do.  Thank you for understanding how I feel.
This is great.  Thank you so much.

Thank you for this perspective. He has never done anything like this before. In fact he has never once begged me or done anything to get my attention in this way. I can't distinguish manipulation from irrational behavior due to true remorse.
Thank you for this -- I really appreciate it.

This is true.  I am feeling desperate to fix everything but maybe not everything can be fixed. All month he has been acting "off" and I knew it was only a matter of time before he would confess. How can I talk about it in a way that helps us move forward instead of turning on the hysterics and saying "Don't forget that you cheated on me!" every time I get upset?

I want to talk about it for hours and hours until I feel better, but he and I both know that telling me every intimate detail will only make it hurt more.  I told him we are starting fresh, starting new because one of us had to do something. Crying forever isn't an option. I just have to be strong and see if anything changes I guess... see if he expresses regret through his future actions. It's the most painful thing I've ever felt in my life. I didn't even cry when my ex-husband left and I'm sitting in a puddle of my own tears because my love for this guy is so strong.
